findings.title: Upsampling tests assert exact upsampled counts (10) but never verify the non-upsampled path returns the raw count for the same data, and rely on cross-project bucket placement that may be flaky
findings.body: In `test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects`, the two events are stored in different projects (`self.project` and `self.project2`) at `day_ago + 1 minute` and `day_ago + 1 hour 1 minute`, and the test asserts `data[0][1][0]['count'] == 10` and `data[1][1][0]['count'] == 10`. This assumes both events land in separate hourly buckets and that `sample_weight = 1/0.1 = 10` is written by the ingest path from the factory's `sample_rate` — but the factory change sets `normalized_data['sample_rate']`, and whether Snuba's `sample_weight` column actually becomes 10 depends on the event-processing pipeline honoring `sample_rate` for error events in the test environment. If the pipeline does not propagate it, the test would fail; if it does, the assertion is correct but brittle. More importantly, the test does not assert the raw-count baseline for identical data without the allowlist in the same test class with the same events (it does in other tests, but with the mock returning `[]` — which also short-circuits before the cache). A direct A/B assertion (same events, allowlist on vs off) would pin the 10x behavior.

findings.title: Allowlist option is compared against raw project IDs but the option value type is not validated
findings.body: `options.get("issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist", [])` is assumed to be a list of ints comparable to `project_id in allowlist`. If an operator configures the option with string IDs (e.g. `["123"]`), the membership check silently fails for every project, disabling upsampling with no error or log. The code should coerce/validate the option (e.g. `{int(p) for p in allowlist}` with a guard) or at least log a warning when the allowlist is non-empty but matches zero projects, so misconfiguration is discoverable.

findings.title: A git submodule pointer file `sentry-repo` was accidentally added at the repository root
findings.body: The PR adds a new top-level file `sentry-repo` containing `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`. This is a git submodule gitlink artifact (typically produced by an accidental `git add` of a nested repo or a submodule update in the wrong directory), not a source file. It should not be committed; it will confuse tooling, CI checkout logic, and reviewers, and it pins a commit hash unrelated to this change. Remove the file and ensure `.gitmodules`/submodule state is unchanged.
